evals.prompt: We are migrating a 35 TB Teradata 17.10 enterprise data warehouse to Amazon Redshift (RA3 / Redshift Serverless) and want to apply `/aws-analytics:redshift-optimize` physical design principles. How do we map Teradata `PRIMARY INDEX` (`UPI`/`NUPI`), Partitioned Primary Index (`PPI`), `SET` vs `MULTISET` tables, `QUALIFY` clauses, and BTEQ / FastLoad / MultiLoad scripts into Redshift?
evals.expected_output: Principal-architect Teradata-to-Redshift migration mapping (`references/teradata/architecture-mapping.md`, `references/teradata/conversion-rules.md`, `references/teradata/etl-and-scripts.md`) covering UPI/NUPI -> `DISTKEY`, PPI -> compound `SORTKEY`, `SET` table deduplication in ETL, `QUALIFY` support, and BTEQ/FastLoad -> Redshift `COPY` + RSQL / Step Functions / Glue.
expectations: Maps Teradata `PRIMARY INDEX` (`UPI` / `NUPI`) to Redshift `DISTSTYLE KEY` (`DISTKEY` on high-cardinality join column) or `DISTSTYLE AUTO`/`ALL`, and maps Teradata Partitioned Primary Index (`PPI`) to Redshift compound `SORTKEY` (`references/teradata/architecture-mapping.md`).

Explains that Redshift does not enforce Teradata `SET` table row-level uniqueness or Primary Key constraints at write time, requiring explicit deduplication (`ROW_NUMBER()` / `QUALIFY` or `MERGE` staging pattern per `references/teradata/conversion-rules.md`).

Maps Teradata utilities: FastLoad / MultiLoad / TPT -> S3 + `COPY` (manifest-based parallel Parquet/CSV loads), and BTEQ scripts -> Amazon Redshift RSQL (`rsql`) or stored procedures orchestrated by Step Functions / MWAA (`references/teradata/bteq-to-rsql.md` and `references/teradata/data-migration-patterns.md`).
Applies the skill's two-pass migration approach: Mechanical Conversion Pass (syntactic DDL/SQL translation) followed by Physical Design Optimization Pass (`DISTSTYLE`/`SORTKEY`/encoding tuning).

Provides clear criteria for data movement: S3 Parquet `COPY` / SCT Extraction Agents for multi-TB historical bulk loads vs AWS DMS for ongoing CDC delta replication during parallel run (`references/oracle/etl-and-tools.md`, `references/sqlserver/etl-and-ssis.md`).

evals.prompt: To migrate our 20 TB Oracle table to Redshift, we plan to execute 500 million single-row `INSERT INTO fact_sales VALUES (...)` statements over JDBC in a Python `for` loop, define an `INTERLEAVED SORTKEY` on `order_timestamp` (which increases monotonically every day), and use `ENCODE RAW` on all 80 non-sort columns. Is this ready for production?
evals.expected_output: Strong architectural pushback explaining why single-row `INSERT`s on a columnar warehouse, `INTERLEAVED SORTKEY` on a monotonically increasing timestamp, and `ENCODE RAW` on all columns are severe Redshift anti-patterns, recommending staged S3 Parquet `COPY`, `COMPOUND SORTKEY`, and `AZ64`/`ZSTD` compression instead.
expectations: Pushes back against single-row JDBC `INSERT` loops on Redshift (each `INSERT` allocates 1 MB minimum columnar blocks and triggers extreme commit overhead), recommending parallel `COPY` from split S3 Parquet/gzip files.

Pushes back against using an `INTERLEAVED SORTKEY` on a monotonically increasing `order_timestamp` column (which causes costly `VACUUM REINDEX` overhead without multi-dimensional filter benefit), recommending a `COMPOUND SORTKEY` with `order_timestamp` first.

Pushes back against `ENCODE RAW` on non-sort columns, recommending `AZ64` for numeric/date/timestamp columns and `ZSTD` / `LZO` for `VARCHAR` columns (leaving only the leading sort key column uncompressed `RAW`).
